decisions.location: Introduction empirical association attribution and References12/14
decisions.quote: In late 2009, xenotropic murine leukemia virus-related virus (XMRV), a recently discovered retrovirus, was detected in the blood of 68% of patients with CFS ( 12 ).
decisions.reason: The complete current report identifies the empirical CFS association as Lombardi et al.2009, reference12, and explicitly re-tests that association with newly collected observations including fresh samples from earlier participants. Reference14 is the2010Mikovits addendum cited for a methodological sensitivity claim. The existing row title was conflated with addendum identifiers and mispaired to the distinct Lo2010target0. Correct existing1106to the explicitly identified2009association paper and target1. This does not require declaring every result or analysis in the addendum equivalent to the Science paper. No primary2009body completeness or analytic equivalence is asserted. The current explicit reference-specific attribution is sufficient to select its tested published empirical finding; date/DOI differences alone are not the reason.

decisions.quote: Our findings do not support an association between CFS and MLV-related viruses, including XMRV, and the off-label use of antiretrovirals for the treatment of CFS does not seem justified at present.
decisions.reason: With existing1106bound to Lombardi2009reference12, the current authors explicitly reject that empirical CFS association in their overall summary and compare their negative results with the positive original and freshly resampled original-cohort participants. Outcome failed follows that named empirical finding. Fresh observations from prior participants do not constitute re-analysis of the old measurements. The negative association result does not establish a ranking of diagnostic methods or independently refute the addendum methodological sensitivity claim; that overbroad clause in the raw expert reason is not adopted. Lo2010reference11is a distinct tested report whose separate candidate scope is preserved.

raw_candidate_expert_opinion.location: Introduction, line 1 (and References 12 and 14, lines 34-37 and 40-43)
raw_candidate_expert_opinion.quote: In conjunction with a third-party phlebotomy service, we also collected samples in a blind manner (blinded samples) from 14 patients in the cohort used in the original CFS-XMRV study performed at the Whittemore Peterson Institute (WPI) ( 12 ). For virus detection, we utilized four different TaqMan quantitative PCR (qPCR) assays, PCR assays that had resulted in the detection of XMRV or MLV-like sequences in previous studies ( 11 , 12 ), and an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) to look for XMRV sequences and antibodies in all of our samples. A subset of samples was analyzed by Western blotting. Using some of the samples, we also attempted to grow virus in a cell culture, a technique outlined in the original study ( 12 ) which, though labor-intensive, has been proposed to be the most sensitive method for viral detection ( 14 ).
raw_candidate_expert_opinion.reason: No prior adjudication or state file exists for this work. Candidate target_index 1 is Lombardi V. C., et al. (2009), 'Detection of an infectious retrovirus, XMRV, in blood cells of patients with chronic fatigue syndrome', Science 326:585-589 (Ref. 12). The sole shipped row (input_row_index '1106', Mikovits; Lombardi; Pfost; Hagen; Ruscetti, 2010, Virulence 1(5):386-390, DOI 10.4161/viru.1.5.12486, Ref. 14) carries the exact same title ('Detection of an infectious retrovirus, XMRV, in blood cells of patients with chronic fatigue syndrome') by the same Whittemore Peterson Institute / NCI author group and is the Virulence companion addendum to Lombardi et al. (2009) elaborating on the cell-culture viral detection assay from the original WPI XMRV-in-CFS study. Because Ref. 12 and shipped row '1106' (Ref. 14) are alternate/addendum reports of the same original WPI XMRV-in-CFS study and finding, target_index 1 is already represented by shipped input_row_index '1106'.
